notes: Access: direct fetch worked throughout, no blocking encountered (curl_cffi/impersonation, Jina, translate.goog never needed). robots.txt lists ClaudeBot/anthropic-ai/Claude-Web alongside GPTBot/PerplexityBot/etc in one AI-crawler group, but that group's Disallow list (/all-products, /p/s/*, /customer*, /sso/*, /c/*, /products/*, /collections/*, /api/*) is IDENTICAL to the generic 'User-agent: *' block (plus an extra Allow: /llms.txt) -- it is not more restrictive for Claude than for any other crawler, and none of the disallowed path prefixes match this site's actual category URL pattern (flat slugs off the root, e.g. /orologi/, /vasi/), so this is not the Claude-specific-disallow case Rule 3 warns about; proceeded. Platform: same custom Shopify Oxygen/Hydrogen storefront family as Westwing UK (c99.json) and Westwing DE (c112.json) -- shared oxygen-v2 asset path family and Shopify Product/ProductVariant GIDs. INDEPENDENCE CHECK (per batch note, done before extracting): (1) IT's own /sitemap-categories.xml has 567 URLs, distinct from DE's 574 and UK's 537 -- three different category-tree sizes, not a mirrored file. (2) EUR pricing throughout (not distinguishing on its own). (3) Did a product-ID overlap check against DE for two categories: Clocks (Orologi/Uhren) -- IT and DE both report exactly 26 products, and a full Shopify ProductVariant-GID comparison found 26/26 IDENTICAL IDs (100% overlap, same specific products). Ceiling Lights (Lampade da soffitto/Deckenleuchten) -- IT 216 vs DE 217, and a 120-item rendered-batch GID comparison found 98/120 (82%) overlap, with distinct IT-only and DE-only product IDs present on each side and different display ordering. CONCLUSION: Westwing IT is a genuine separate storefront (own domain, own currency display, own qty numbers, own canonical URLs, own product subset) but its assortment overlaps DE's very heavily -- far more than DE overlapped with UK in the prior extraction (DE vs UK differed by double-digit percentages on nearly every shared category, e.g. Ceiling Lights 217 DE vs 192 UK). Roughly two dozen of this file's categories returned counts within 0-1 of DE's exact figure (Desk Lamps 89=89, Clocks 26=26 with 100% ID match, Canvas Art 130=130, Framed Art 63=63, Posters 92=92, Acoustic Wall Art 12=12, Picture Frames 59=59, Decorative Wall Objects 36=36, Ornaments 156=156, Decorative Bowls 144=144, Decorative Trays 137=137, Bookends 24=24, Candlesticks & Candle Holders 199=199, Candles 143=143, Tealight Holders 21=21, LED Candles 21=21, Lanterns 43=43, Teapots 29=29, Serving Platters 188=188, Cake Stands 53=53, Aperitif Bowls 33=33, Milk Jugs & Sugar Bowls 34=34, Egg Cups 37=37, Serving Trays 49=49, Coasters 55=55, Napkin Holders 41=41, Fairy Lights 3=3, Floor Lamps 199=199), which reads as two Eurozone markets (DE, IT) drawing on a heavily-shared supplier catalogue while the smaller/most-divergent lighting categories (Pendant Lights 500 vs DE 501, Chandeliers 44=44, Wall Lights 323 vs 324, Table Lamps 634 vs 635, Bedside Lamps 627 vs 628) track within single digits of DE too -- consistent with same-catalogue-different-market rather than coincidence, but the Ceiling Lights 82%-not-100% ID check and the differing sitemap sizes confirm this is a real independent IT storefront, not a redirect or literal duplicate of c112.json. Extracted IT's own rows with IT's own qty/links throughout, and flagged this overlap explicitly rather than silently assuming duplication or independence either way, per the batch instruction. Qty verified via the page's own rendered 'N Prodotti' text, which appears twice per page at two independent DOM locations (a sort/filter-bar count label and a mobile filter-panel label) with an identical value in a single fetch -- cross-checked on Orologi (Clocks) where the wishlist-button tile count on the page (26) also matched the header exactly, confirming full-page render for smaller categories; larger categories only SSR-render an initial batch (e.g. Vasi/Vases showed 456 in the header text but only 120 product tiles in the initial HTML), so for those the rendered 'N Prodotti' header text itself (appearing twice, identically) is the qty of record, consistent with the DE/UK precedent method in this project. Site nav discovered via the homepage's embedded Remix/Hydrogen loader JSON (menu label/href pairs extracted with regex) cross-checked against /sitemap-categories.xml; used the current mega-nav URLs (e.g. /specchi-2/, /specchi-da-parete-3/) over older same-name sitemap-only URLs (e.g. /specchi/, /specchi-da-parete/) which returned DIFFERENT (not identical) counts on the same product type -- treated the sitemap-only duplicates as legacy/orphaned collections not linked from live navigation and excluded them to avoid padding with a stale facet. three already-excluded kitchen-tool nodes Macinaspezie/Olio-Aceto/Accessori da Bar, so it is a mixed/kitchen-tool roll-up, dropped entirely with no row per 'mixed roll-ups: drop them, don't pad'). Rule 0 gains: full Outdoor Lighting branch kept (Outdoor Wall/Table/Floor/Pendant Lights, 4 leaves, 368 combined units) despite the room word; Bedside Lamps and Kids Lighting kept despite room words; Full-Length, Floor and Makeup Mirrors kept alongside Wall Mirrors despite being bathroom/bedroom-adjacent fixture types; conversely 'Decorazioni Bagno' was correctly EXCLUDED after Rule 0 product-type inspection showed it to be storage hardware wearing a decor-sounding name, the inverse case Rule 0 also guards against (don't include just because a room-labelled node sounds decorative -- check the product type).
